Consider the maximally correlated state canonically identified with

    G_p = (1-p) I_d/d + p |+><+|,       0 <= p <= 1.

Let F=(1+(d-1)p)/d, gamma(F)=(sqrt(F)+sqrt((d-1)(1-F)))^2/d and

    R(F) = h_2(gamma(F)) + (1-gamma(F)) log_2(d-1).

Its formation is exactly the convex hull co R(F). For d>2 this is R(F) through F=4(d-1)/d^2, followed by the line

    log_2 d + [d log_2(d-1)/(d-2)] (F-1).

For d=2 use R(F) everywhere. Distillable entanglement is exactly log_2 d - S(G_p).

Reason for the exact formation reduction: isotropic LOCC twirling of the associated MC state retains maximally entangled fraction F, giving the usual isotropic-state formation as a lower bound. Conversely, the isotropic minimizing pure Schmidt vector, with one distinguished nonnegative amplitude and all other amplitudes equal, can be twirled by simultaneous basis permutations. Its MC Gram state is exactly G_p. Mixtures achieve the convex hull. Thus both bounds coincide.

Primary sources for the scalar convex-roof minimization and its convex hull:
- Terhal and Vollbrecht, https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0005062
- Fei and Li-Jost (proof of the all-dimensional convex-hull formula), https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0602137

### Covariant squashing family

A pure output vector phi_i on (d+1)x(d+1) has amplitudes constant on the ten orbits of simultaneous label permutations fixing i. The first five orbits are (j=k=i), (j=i != k), (k=i != j), (j=k != i), and (j,k,i all distinct). The last five involve an extra invariant basis vector indexed d: (d,d), (d,i), (d,j != i), (i,d), (j != i,d).

Assign arbitrary complex amplitudes to these ten orbits and normalize. Their pairwise overlaps are a common real p, so their uniform Gram state is G_p. This gives a twenty-real-parameter structured quantum squashing, with output dimensions d+1 and d+1, and a rigorously evaluable formation benchmark for p>=0.

Script: search_pyramid_squash.py. Seed 20261009; 25 BFGS starts for each d=3,4,6,8,12, maxiter 250. Objective:

    chi(B)+chi(E)-S(G_p)-[log d - E_F(G_p)].

All 125 runs failed to find a positive value; maxima approached the uninformative p=1 boundary. This does not rule out interior local maxima or larger representations. The code uses the weaker E_F>=0 rather than an exact formula when p<0; therefore negative-p points were not properly tested for exclusion. Full log: pyramid_search.log. Best numerical

# Testing the new reconstruction theorem against correlated measurement de Finetti

9 October 2026 UTC. A concrete named-problem transfer attempt, with an exact obstruction to the attempted bridge. No claim of solving or refuting the conjecture.

## Named primary target and status boundary

Brandão and Harrow, Quantum de Finetti Theorems under Local Measurements with Applications, arXiv:1210.6367v5, Conjecture 5, equations (12)–(13), printed pp.12–13, explicitly proposes:

For a k-extendible state ρ_AB and output dimension D=dim(A_tilde), find ONE separable σ_AB such that

max_(E:A→A_tilde) max_(measurement Λ:B→classical)
||(E⊗Λ)(ρ_AB−σ_AB)||₁ ≤ sqrt(2lnD/k).

The equivalent averaged formulation permits the receiver measurement to depend on the chosen compression E_m. The proven theorem in that paper has the expectation and measurement maximization in the opposite order. The authors explicitly identify this as a different quantum problem, not a no-signaling information-chain corollary.

Primary: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1210.6367

The conjecture is verified as a named proposal in the original primary source. A targeted search for a later resolution did not locate one, but did not establish its current 2026 open status conclusively. Therefore it is not described here as a newly verified longstanding open problem. Its old complexity consequences also must not be restated as current novelty without accounting for later nonlocal-game results.

## Why the new machinery initially looks relevant

The bounded-capacity reconstruction theorem now gives one common EB channel uniformly over all promised states, not a separate measurement for each observable. It also handles arbitrary trace norm rather than only a measured residual. These are superficially similar to the missing common-separable-state and correlated-measurement requirements.

For each fixed compression E:A→A_tilde, a conditional-state experiment on A_tilde has capacity at most lnD. A k-extension supplies many correlated B registers. It is tempting to try to turn these ingredients into a small-error broadcaster and apply the new theorem.
